items.issues: Timing (eyesight news → same week) plus loosened honey lid (scent) fix C; D (apology) is the nearest runner-up but lacks a textual trigger.
Second sweep under her chair + clasp fastened = narrator ceding the place; D (nostalgic) tempting but no retrospective frame.
Bell set mouth down where steam reaches at the old hour settles C; A/D read only the surface laughter and polite thanks.
Ledger with every line crossed through makes B nearly explicit; less inference than requested hard.
Open case toward door + still copying Irena's bowings + leading tuning give the dual pull; C (vibration felt by ensemble) is the strong attribute-based distractor.
'On the latch' idiom plus the tea cup placed nearest the narrator make B fairly direct; D undermined by her short answers to aunts being a different register.
Nightly ledger ritual, date written 'not a payment' anchor C; B (shame) is the best distractor but he does not avoid her.
Routine actions + 'even voice' + still confronting the surveyor exclude A/C/D; B is the only one fitting both restraint and action.
Wearing the sweater sweating and still conjugating years later outweigh the complaints; D is the closest runner-up but 'patience' undersells the ending.
C is the only option linking the aunt's silence to the handmade pan; others are partial or causal reversals.
Tags 'K. and H.' plus pegging shirts beside hers is the answer-in-place-of-apology; B is a flat literal reading, C misattributes the quarrel.
'Never once after him' + photograph of father raking that basin make A; C is a partial detail, D a causal inversion.
Chalked date kept, skiff, and ticket punch on far bank settle D; A is the surface excuse; B contradicted by her rowing him across anyway.
Keeping the seed envelope and checking the seal yearly points gratitude at Anders specifically; D (the years/place) is the nearest distractor.
'Señora' as for the baker + thicker envelope and flat apron pocket fix A; B accepts only the surface formality.
Chalk back in tin and lifting the bowl across himself; C overreads ('lost friendship' not in text), B lacks support.
Drawing the plate back three times then moving in once pudding is pushed toward him; D (sailor habit) exploits the vehicle's imagery; B contradicted by ending.
Daily approach and turning back, pocket re-buttoned at the end; C (duty ordering his days) is the strongest wrong answer, B adds external obstacle not in text.
Last wage paid, clearing crew due, keys left on the nail exclude C; A is fixed by 'already moored'.
Other three scholars' Memphis/Chicago addresses + the ever-lowering pool make the draining reading; D is the literal-vehicle distractor; A ignores the loss.
